stations.title: Seizure — Status Epilepticus
stations.task: Manage a patient presenting with ongoing generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting more than 5 minutes

patient.name: Michael Brown
patient.opening: (Actively seizing on arrival — generalized tonic-clonic activity for 8 minutes)

mustAsk: Has the patient had seizures before?

questions.question: What is the first-line treatment for established status epilepticus?
questions.answer: IV lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg (or midazolam IM if no IV access)

stations.title: Peripheral Neuropathy Evaluation
stations.task: Evaluate a patient with progressive bilateral lower extremity numbness and weakness

patient.name: Helen Davis
patient.opening: Doctor, my feet have been numb for months and now I'm starting to trip when I walk.

keySymptoms: Progressive bilateral leg numbness over 6 months

bonus: Ask about family history of neuropathy
Inquire about balance and fall risk

questions.question: What nerve conduction study finding distinguishes CIDP from diabetic neuropathy?
questions.answer: Prolonged distal motor latencies and conduction block (demyelinating pattern)
